claims.claim: The Lean 4 corpus proves that the Maxwell/Trinity isomorphism satisfies five formal conditions simultaneously, while five specific false positives (Heaviside EM, modalism, static single-field EM, generic 3-part system) are rejected under the same gate.
claims.plain_english: The computer checked that the math of electromagnetism and the Christian Trinity have the same structure, and it also checked that other similar ideas do not match.
claims.evidence_given: 287 named theorems, zero sorry/admit, 5 false positives tested and rejected, every guard load-bearing.
claims.what_would_break_it: If any of the five false positives actually satisfied all five conditions, or if the formal model of Maxwell EM or Nicene Trinity was shown to be unfaithful to the originals.

claims.claim: The Justice/Mercy operator proves by exhaustive case elimination that the Cross is the unique configuration satisfying all five conditions for perfect moral repair (proportional justice, impartiality, truth-naming, victim restoration, voluntary cost-bearing).
claims.plain_english: The computer proved that only the Christian Cross meets all five requirements for making things right after wrongdoing, and every other option fails at least one requirement.
claims.evidence_given: Theorem 125 (cross_is_unique_solution) with exhaustive cases proof; theorems 118-124 show alternatives fail.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a counterexample configuration satisfying all five conditions but not the Cross were found, or if the five conditions are not the correct formalization of perfect moral repair.

claims.claim: The Master Equation is domain-neutral: χ(physical) = χ(spiritual) under the canonical variable map, meaning the same coherence equation applies to both physics and theology without belonging to either register.
claims.plain_english: The same math formula works for both physical and spiritual ideas, so the formula itself doesn't favor science or religion.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a valid assignment of physical variables produced a different coherence value than the corresponding spiritual assignment under the canonical map.

claims.claim: The zero-collapse architecture (Theorem 4) proves that if any single factor (will, knowledge, etc.) is zero, total coherence collapses to zero regardless of all other factors — no compensation is possible.
claims.plain_english: If any one essential ingredient is missing, the whole thing fails completely, no matter how strong the other ingredients are.
claims.evidence_given: Theorem 4 (Q_zero_collapses_chi) in Core.lean; the multiplicative architecture is explicitly contrasted with additive frameworks.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a counterexample showed nonzero coherence when one factor is zero, or if the multiplicative model is not the correct formalization.

claims.claim: The sign conversion discipline (Theorems 133-136) proves that in the moral burden domain, two negatives stay negative — accumulation does not redeem — and only external Christic conversion flips a negative burden to positive.
claims.plain_english: In the math of moral debt, doing two bad things doesn't cancel out; only an outside source can turn a negative into a positive.
claims.evidence_given: Theorems 133-136 in SignConversionDiscipline.lean; Lean-backed foundation for why the Cross is structurally necessary.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a self-generated operation (not external) could change the sign of a negative burden, or if the arithmetic model does not correctly represent moral burden.

claims.claim: The resurrection architecture (Theorems 153-162) proves that substrate identity is preserved through incarnation, death, and resurrection, but the post-resurrection state carries entropy and death contact records — making it richer than the pre-incarnate state, not identical to it.
claims.plain_english: The computer model shows that the same person goes through life, death, and resurrection, but comes back with evidence of having died, so it's not just a reset.
claims.evidence_given: Theorems 153-162 in MissionReturnOperator.lean; identity preserved, entropy and death contact carried through, resurrection is not reset.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the formal model allowed identity to change across the arc, or if resurrection could be shown to be a reset to pre-incarnate state.

claims.claim: The corpus has 287 theorems with zero sorry/admit, meaning the machine verified every logical step — but this does not mean the real world matches the model; domain judgment and empirical evidence are separate.
claims.plain_english: The computer checked all the math and found no errors, but that doesn't prove the math matches reality — that's a different question for experts and experiments.
claims.evidence_given: Stats row: 287 named theorems, 0 sorry/admit, 16 Lean files, 70+ adversarial rejections, 80% bridge hit rate.
claims.what_would_break_it: If any theorem contained a logical error not caught by Lean, or if the formal definitions are not faithful to the real-world concepts they model.

claims.claim: The corpus names its own gaps (GAP-01 through GAP-05, SPEC-01, SPEC-03, SPEC-05) — including that historical claims about Jesus of Nazareth are outside Lean's scope and require separate historical evidence.
claims.plain_english: The project honestly admits what it hasn't proved yet, including that the computer can't tell you if Jesus really existed or did what the Bible says.
claims.evidence_given: Table of named gaps with descriptions and status (closable vs. spec gap).
claims.what_would_break_it: If a gap were later shown to be mischaracterized or if the system claimed more than it proved.

claims.claim: The Strong Force ≅ Love isomorphism (Theorems 78-87) passes at the RichLawIso level (roles AND transitions preserved), while a coin model fails at that level — proving the mapping is nontrivial.
claims.plain_english: The computer checked that the strong nuclear force and love have the same deep structure, and a simple coin model doesn't match, so the connection is meaningful.
claims.evidence_given: Theorems 78-87 in IsomorphismTest.lean; two-level isomorphism with adversarial false-positive testing; coin model eliminated.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the coin model actually passed at the RichLawIso level, or if the formal model of StrongForce or Love is unfaithful.

claims.claim: The polarity discipline (L2-Q6) proves that good is ontologically prior: positive is generative, negative is parasitic, and evil has no independent vocabulary — it borrows every word from good and inverts it.
claims.plain_english: The math shows that good comes first and evil can only twist what already exists; evil can't create anything new on its own.
claims.evidence_given: Theorem L2-Q6 in PolarityDiscipline.lean; sign arithmetic enforces asymmetry.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a counterexample showed evil having an independent generative vocabulary, or if the model's asymmetry does not reflect real-world moral ontology.
